# Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map

## Original exercise

Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.

> 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
> with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
> \[
> \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
>       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
> \]

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

1: # Shared-lemma extraction as a local NL0 revision
2: 
3: ## Scope and position
4: 
5: Apply this procedure at the start of **NL0-to-Lean translation**, before final
6: interface/planning freeze or worker-packet generation. It is not an extra
7: requirement for a task that requests NL0 alone. The input is an existing,
8: versioned NL0, not an invitation to reconstruct its proof.
9: 
10: The operation is proof factoring: move an already supplied local derivation
11: into one shared N/R pair and replace its occurrences by explicit applications.
12: Do not rewrite the whole NL0, regenerate its prose, reprove unchanged results,
13: or seek a stronger/general theorem for speculative future reuse. Reading the
14: existing graph to locate candidates is not a new proof-construction task.
15: If an existing N already exports the needed fact, reuse that node directly.
16: 
17: Use [the revision record](../templates/source-refactoring.md). Preserve the
18: original package and audit as immutable evidence. Write a revised package in
19: a new directory; retain existing IDs and keep the revision identity in the
20: sidecar record. Generated Markdown/diagrams are views, never patch authorities.
21: 
22: ## 1. Locate and qualify candidates without reconstructing NL0
23: 
24: Start with existing node statements, direct inputs, definitions and any
25: available index. Locate repeated subarguments using their mathematical role,
26: objects, formulas or operation names; then inspect the actual candidate spans
27: and the local context they need. Do not commission a new proof or a full prose
28: summary for every node as a discovery method. Text similarity is only a lead.
29: 
30: For each proposed lemma record:
31: 
32: - The complete mathematical statement, all parameters/conditions and proposed
33:   direct input IDs, together with exact old graph pointers or paragraph spans.
34: - The existing derivation to reuse and every occurrence that will consume it.
35:   The derivation must actually supply the proposed statement; a summary label
36:   or a theorem believed true from memory is insufficient.
37: - Identify the baseline revision/old paragraph IDs separately from the current
38:   new producer. A new N's origin label must state the historical/current
39:   distinction; a bare old R number is ambiguous after consumer editing.
40: - The expected avoided repeated work. An occurrence count is not measured
41:   formalization cost and does not by itself establish a speed benefit.
42: - The scope at each occurrence, including bound variables, temporary
43:   assumptions, definition guards and local facts established before the span.
44: 
45: Prefer a statement already justified at the cuts. Do not generalize its domain,
46: change representations, weaken conditions or introduce new mathematics merely
47: to make more occurrences match. If the proposed derivation needs an earlier
48: local calculation, include that calculation with its justified inputs. Never
49: declare an unexported local fact to be an available graph input.
50: 
51: Temporary assumptions stay closed in an implication or other complete
52: proposition; they cannot become H roots. An extraction that moves a witness,
53: choice, definition or binder across a scope boundary needs an explicit account
54: of the values and properties used afterwards. If that account cannot be made
55: locally and clearly, leave the original argument in place.
56: 
57: ## 2. Write the patch boundary before editing
58: 
59: Prepare an edit allowlist for one candidate or one coherent batch:
60: 
61: | Part | Allowed edit |
62: | --- | --- |
63: | New shared theorem | One fresh N and its R producer, with a complete statement and derivation from existing permitted inputs. |
64: | Actual consumers | Replace only the located repeated proof spans by a complete application; adjust direct inputs, citations and application accounting accordingly. |
65: | Necessary local bookkeeping | Update the directly affected binder/reference accounting and generated views. Record every such edit explicitly. |
66: | Everything else | Preserve the existing record content; do not reorder or renumber it as a cleanup. |
67: 
68: Keep the entire frozen specification unchanged: target P, original H, parameter
69: domains, global definitions/notation, logic, pins and E/M source inventories and
70: statements. Preserve all existing N/P statements and every unmodified argument
71: span. New sources, changed hypotheses, new global definitions, removed existing
72: nodes, or a changed old output are outside this fast factoring operation.
73: 
74: Copy an existing derivation rather than writing a new proof route. The new
75: producer may use only its declared inputs, global definitions and legitimate
76: local derivations. It cannot depend on a consumer output or its descendants.
77: Do not split each consumer into additional source nodes around the shared fact.
78: 
79: Each consumer application must state the parameter substitution, which inputs
80: or local proved facts discharge each condition, and the exact conclusion used.
81: Remove a former direct input only if the remaining argument no longer uses it;
82: retain it when it still has a direct role. A shared theorem is never ambient.
83: 
84: If an edit escapes the allowlist, return that candidate to the shortlist or
85: leave it unextracted. A source defect goes through the existing gap procedure;
86: do not turn a reuse optimization into a repair or a new research route.
87: 
88: ## 3. Check structural preservation globally, reasoning locally
89: 
90: Compare canonical JSON records by stable IDs, not only rendered text or changed
91: line numbers. Record before/after hashes and the actual changed fields/spans.
92: Reject any unexplained diff. Check these global mechanical invariants:
93: 
94: - The frozen specification and protected records are unchanged.
95: - All IDs/references resolve; definitions and guards remain available; there
96:   is no cycle or unsupported initial node; every N/P still has one producer.
97: - Every retained node remains in P's dependency closure. Reject the candidate
98:   if it would require deleting or reorganizing unrelated nodes to restore this.
99: - All consumers declare their actual inputs and remain self-contained. Only
100:   the explicit allowlisted nodes/fields have changed.
101: 
102: Run the existing `../scripts/nl0.py check` on the revised graph and specification.
103: Rechecking graph metadata across the package is allowed and inexpensive relative
104: to rereading every mathematical proof. It does not require a new LLM proof of
105: every node, and it does not establish the semantics of a substitution.
106: 
107: Distinguish **review impact** from **dependency status**. The new producer and
108: edited application boundaries need new mathematical review. An unchanged
109: downstream proof whose input statements and conventions are unchanged need not
110: be reconstructed merely because its ancestors have a new producer. Its final
111: acceptance nevertheless depends on the replacement producer being accepted.
112: Until that happens, affected descendants are pending, not newly accepted.
113: 
114: ## 4. Incremental Audit A: review the new proof and the substitution cuts
115: 
116: This is an incremental review procedure under Audit A's mathematical
117: obligations, not permission to weaken source verification or invent a fresh
118: packet replay. The version-bound receipt limitation below is part of the rule.
119: 
120: First inspect the baseline audit and its evidence bindings. Reuse a judgment
121: only for the exact previously reviewed content, context and evidence. Carry
122: FAIL, UNVERIFIED, inaccessible sources and disclosure limits forward. A source
123: file hash proves byte identity, not that an auditor ever inspected the theorem.
124: An unaudited baseline cannot acquire whole-proof acceptance through extraction.
125: 
126: Review the **new N/R in full**: complete statement, exact inputs, argument,
127: dependency accounting, scopes, guards and E/M applications, and the normal
128: fresh packet-only replay requirement. The extracted proof may be copied, but
129: its new closed interface and context must actually be checked.
130: 
131: For **each changed consumer**, review a substitution cut rather than rewriting
132: or replaying its entire old proof by default:
133: 
134: 1. Compare the old derived conclusion at the cut with the instantiated shared
135:    result, including all conditions, quantifiers and semantic conventions.
136: 2. Check that every condition of the shared theorem follows from that consumer's
137:    declared inputs or explicit in-scope local derivations, without extra facts.
138: 3. Check the interface to the untouched continuation: every subsequently used
139:    proposition, object, value and scope remains available with the same meaning.
140:    Equal output text alone cannot establish preservation of a selected witness.
141: 4. Verify the changed direct-input/citation/application accounting. Reuse source
142:    identity evidence only when unchanged; check every new source application.
143: 5. Bind the untouched remainder to its old reviewed bytes and old review
144:    evidence. Record exactly which old checks are inherited and which new checks
145:    cover the patch. Do not relabel this comparison as a new fresh whole-R replay.
146: 
147: If those boundaries do not justify inheritance, mark that candidate
148: `DEFERRED_NOT_LOCAL` and keep the baseline argument. Do not automatically expand
149: to a full-case audit. A separately requested broader review may inspect the
150: specific unresolved node, but is not part of this fast extraction.
151: 
152: Unchanged target/source/definition reviews and proof regions need no new
153: mathematical re-review when their audited content, applicable context and
154: evidence are unchanged. Do not reopen source searches solely because a global
155: graph hash changed. Changes or failures in their evidence invalidate reuse.
156: 
157: The result is a chain: baseline audit + exact revision + actual new reviews.
158: It is not a copied PASS with an updated graph hash. Record actual reviewer
159: exposure; old-review access is appropriate for delta review and cannot be called
160: an independent fresh packet-only review. This procedure authorizes no additional
161: agent or external-service dispatch.
162: 
163: ## 5. Seal or leave the candidate unextracted
164: 
165: Seal only after the allowlist/diff and graph checks pass and the scoped
166: mathematical review is complete. Keep original and revised manifests, patch,
167: location map, old/new evidence, pending findings and measured preparation cost.
168: Stage all candidate edits transactionally; a failed candidate must not replace
169: the accepted baseline. Do not launch formalization workers for an unaccepted
170: source revision or reuse task packets bound to the old graph.
171: 
172: Then finalize and freeze typed interfaces, shared Lean ports and local plans;
173: only afterwards generate worker packets. Shared Lean interface discovery may
174: use this preparation pass, but must not silently mutate the sealed NL0 later.
175: No extraction is a valid outcome; do not manufacture shared lemmas to satisfy
176: the workflow. The work is bounded by the chosen proof regions and patch size,
177: not a universal minute count. Longer time alone is not a mathematical gap.
178: 
179: ## Executable acceptance and review responsibilities
180: 
181: The unchanged parent checker still binds ordinary format-4 audit to the complete
182: graph. `scripts/source_preparation.py` adds a separate incremental record;
183: it never copies old PASS fields into a forged fresh whole-graph audit.
184: Audit B and `workflow.py` both revalidate that record and all underlying evidence.
185: See [commands and the patch contract](integrated-workflow.md).
186: 
187: The initial executable scope is current-v2 source and nonoverlapping consumer
188: paragraph substitutions. Old proposition records/specification, unlisted R
189: records, untouched paragraphs and local fact/assumption lifetimes are protected.
190: Consumer source-application changes can remove obsolete uses, not introduce new
191: external uses. A broader refactor is deferred rather than widening this operation.
192: Multiple proposed edits to one consumer must first be merged into one coherent
193: candidate or left unextracted. Legacy test copies remain development evidence.
194: 
195: Separate three responsibilities:
196: 
197: - A producer reviewer sees only the complete new per-R packet and audits its
198:   conditional mathematics under ordinary Audit A, including actual fresh replay.
199:   Do not ask that packet to establish whole-graph acceptance or old-copy provenance.
200: - A substitution reviewer sees paired before/after consumers, the proposed shared
201:   statement, original derivations and explicit cut contract. `old_derivation`
202:   names THIS consumer's replaced proof; `producer_source_derivation` names the
203:   one original proof used to export the shared lemma. Its supplier may be a
204:   different consumer with a different final goal. Compare the common intermediate
205:   conclusion, not equality of those final goals. Check existing-proof
206:   factoring, each condition, exact supplied conclusion, continuation and accounting.
207:   This is delta review with baseline access, not fresh whole-consumer replay.
208: - Python checks canonical fanout, edit scope, graph validity, immutable evidence,
209:   the exact coverage partition and inherited acceptance/qualifications. It does
210:   not judge natural-language mathematics or authenticate a dishonest reviewer.
211: 
212: Internal N applications are direct inputs, paragraph citations and explicit prose;
213: the parent's `applications` source records remain E/M-only. Do not invent an N
214: source-application record to satisfy a reviewer. A prose citation without a real
215: substitution is not successful factoring. Derivation labels and fanout guesses
216: from a model are leads, not canonical graph facts.
217: 
218: Each cut review binds the exact supplied packet hash. Retain the binding from
219: the generated template and verify it during acceptance. Reusing an actual old
220: review after a record-only change requires identical canonical mathematics and
221: byte-identical actual reviewed packets; preserve its verdicts, notes, evidence
222: and original cost, and disclose that no new mathematical review occurred.
223: 
224: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires a passing current baseline plus all actual
225: new producer/cut reviews. Missing/failed baseline checks remain inherited and
226: yield development-only local review. Every later consumer acceptance still
227: depends on the new producer; unchanged input statements and context permit
228: inheriting the old conditional argument without rereading it mathematically.
229: No fixed completion-time threshold makes a candidate worthwhile or incorrect.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary x∈ℝ^n and a real t, temporarily assuming L1: t>0. By H002 the component functions are smooth near (x,t). H004 gives u·u=1 in that neighborhood. Differentiating this identity in time by the componentwise product rule gives 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. All quantities in this paragraph are evaluated at (x,t).
H005 at (x,t) provides a real a with u_tt−Delta u=a u; choose one. By F001 and symmetry of the inner product, u_t·(u_tt−Delta u)=a(u_t·u)=0. No derivative of a has been taken.

The same twice-differentiated unit constraint gives 0=∂_t²(u·u)=2|u_t|²+2u·u_tt, so u·u_tt=−|u_t|². For each spatial coordinate j from 1 through n, differentiating twice in that coordinate gives 0=2|∂_{x_j}u|²+2u·∂_{x_jx_j}u, so u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=−|∂_{x_j}u|². Dotting the chosen normality equation with u and using u·u=1 yields a=u·u_tt−Σ_j u·∂_{x_jx_j}u=Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². This calculation uses only the equation for a, and therefore holds for every real scalar satisfying that equation at this point. Substitution gives u_tt−Delta u=(Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|²)u. Combine this with F001 and F002, discharge L1 to retain t>0 as the quantifier condition, and universally quantify x and t. This proves all the asserted pointwise identities and the explicit equation.

Choose C with u(x,r)=q outside C for every r∈J using F001.
Choose R>0 with C⊂(−R,R)^n as established by F002.
Define Q=[−R,R]^n.

argument.text: Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0. Put J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Its endpoints satisfy 0<t0/2<3t0/2<∞, so H006 provides a compact spatial set for that entire interval. H001 gives finite positive integer dimensions throughout.

produces.statement: There exists compact C⊂ℝ^n with u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and r∈J.

argument.text: Choose such a C from F001. A compact subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space is bounded; enlarging a bound gives a positive real R such that C⊂(−R,R)^n. Compactness also makes C closed, hence (ℝ^n\C)×int J is open. On this open set u=q. By H002 and the local derivative of a constant, every positive-order spatial or time derivative of u vanishes there. Differentiating a constant here uses the fixed vector q and requires no condition on its norm.

produces.statement: All positive-order space/time derivatives of u vanish on (ℝ^n\C)×int J.

argument.text: Choose R as in F002 and put Q=[−R,R]^n. It is compact and has finite Lebesgue measure |Q|=(2R)^n. By smoothness H002, finite sums and products of the derivatives occurring in e, e_t, u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_j}u and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u) are continuous, and e,e_t are jointly smooth. At every fixed r∈int J each listed spatial function vanishes outside C by F003, and is bounded on Q by continuity on a compact set. Continuous real functions on ℝ^n are measurable; a bound on Q and zero values outside Q dominate their absolute values by a finite constant times the indicator of Q. That indicator is integrable with integral (2R)^n, so each function is absolutely integrable. This applies to every spatial coordinate j with 1≤j≤n, and to every r∈int J.

produces.statement: Q has measure (2R)^n<∞. The functions e,e_t are smooth. For every r∈int J and 1≤j≤n, the spatial functions e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, u_t·∂_{x_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), evaluated at r, are continuous, supported in C, measurable, bounded on Q and absolutely integrable.

argument.text: Define η=t0/4>0. Then [t0−η,t0+η]=[3t0/4,5t0/4]⊂(t0/2,3t0/2)=int J. The continuous real function |e_t| on the compact nonempty set Q×[t0−η,t0+η] is bounded. Taking a nonnegative bound proves that there exists B≥0 with |e_t(x,r)|≤B for every x∈Q and every r in this closed time interval.

produces.statement: There exists B≥0 with |e_t(x,r)|≤B for all x∈Q, r∈[t0−η,t0+η], and η>0 with this interval contained in int J.

argument.text: Choose B from F004. The witnesses C,R,η,B and defined J,Q have all the asserted common-support, measure, regularity, integrability and bound properties by F001,F002,F003,F005,F004. In particular t0∈int J and e(·,t0) is integrable. Introduce the existential quantifiers over C,R,η,B before closing their scope; discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary t0. This proves the detailed common-support assertion and, by the arbitrariness of the positive base time, integrability of e(·,t) for every t>0.

argument.text:
Fix real t0 and temporarily assume L1: t0>0. Instantiate N002 to choose jointly C,R,η,B, and set J=[t0/2,3t0/2], Q=[−R,R]^n as in that statement. In particular the indicated time window lies in int J. By H002 the product rule and equality of mixed coordinate derivatives give, at every (x,t) with t>0,
e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_j}u(x,t)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t).
N002 makes every term on the right integrable at each such time.

produces.statement: For all x∈ℝ^n and t>0, e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2Σ_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u(x,t)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t); all summands as spatial functions at each positive time are integrable.

argument.text:
For each fixed spatial point x∈Q and each real nonzero increment h0 with |h0|<η, apply M004 to the real function of time r↦e(x,r), extended by zero on nonpositive times, and its derivative r↦e_t(x,r) on positive times (also assigned zero elsewhere). Use the ordered endpoints min(t0,t0+h0), max(t0,t0+h0). Their closed interval lies inside [t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J, where smoothness gives continuity and the stated derivative. M004 gives an intermediate derivative equal to the secant slope. For either sign of h0 that slope is (e(x,t0+h0)−e(x,t0))/h0. The uniform bound in N002 therefore gives its absolute value at most B. Outside Q both densities are zero by N002. Thus throughout ℝ^n,
|(e(x,t0+h0)−e(x,t0))/h0|≤B 1_Q(x).
The right side is integrable, since Q has finite measure and B is finite and nonnegative.

produces.statement: For all x∈ℝ^n and all real h0 with 0<|h0|<η, |(e(x,t0+h0)−e(x,t0))/h0|≤B 1_Q(x). The function B 1_Q is Lebesgue integrable.

argument.text: Take an arbitrary real sequence h and temporarily assume L2: for every natural k, 0<|h(k)|<η, and h(k)→0. Define V(k)(x)=(e(x,t0+h(k))−e(x,t0))/h(k) and w(x)=B 1_Q(x). Each V(k) is a continuous real function of x, hence strongly measurable and in particular almost everywhere strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure; it is integrable either by N002 and linearity or by F002. By F002, |V(k)(x)|≤w(x) everywhere, and w is integrable. By the pointwise time differentiability supplied by smoothness, V(k)(x)→e_t(x,t0) for every x. All these facts concern the real codomain and the Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n.

produces.statement: Each V(k) is almost everywhere strongly measurable for dx, w is integrable, |V(k)(x)|≤w(x) for every k and x, and V(k)(x)→e_t(x,t0) for every x.

argument.text: Apply M001 with its measure space ℝ^n with Lebesgue measure, codomain ℝ, sequence V, limit x↦e_t(x,t0), and bound w. The four analytic premises were proved in F003, and ℝ has the required real normed-space structure. It follows that ∫ V(k)(x) dx→∫ e_t(x,t0) dx. N002 and D004 identify, by linearity of finite integrals, ∫ V(k)(x) dx=(E(t0+h(k))−E(t0))/h(k). Discharge L2 and quantify the arbitrary sequence h: every sequence of nonzero increments in this punctured η-window tending to zero gives energy quotients tending to ∫ e_t(x,t0) dx.

produces.statement: For every sequence zeta:ℕ→ℝ, if 0<|zeta(k)|<η for every k and zeta(k)→0, then (E(t0+zeta(k))−E(t0))/zeta(k)→∫_{ℝ^n}e_t(x,t0) dx.

argument.text:
F004 implies the full punctured limit as the real increment tends to zero. Indeed failure of that limit would give some fixed positive error and arbitrarily small nonzero increments within the η-window whose quotient errors are at least that amount. Choosing one at distance less than 1/(k+1) for each natural k would form a sequence contradicting F004. This is the sequential criterion for limits in ℝ, with the entire window inside positive time. Thus the actual finite integral E is differentiable at t0 and
E'(t0)=∫_{ℝ^n}e_t(x,t0) dx.
Combine this with F001 and the integrability exported in N002. Discharge L1 and universally quantify t0; no choices C,R,η,B enter the conclusion. This proves the claimed derivative formula and integrability.

hypothesis_checks: H002 and N002 give smoothness and hence continuity on this closed interval, contained in the positive time window.
The time derivative on that interval is e_t by H002 and F001; no extension point at r≤0 lies in the interval.

applications.bindings: Set A=ℝ^n with its Lebesgue measurable space and μ=dx, G=ℝ, source F(k)=V(k), source f(x)=e_t(x,t0), and source bound=w=B 1_Q.
hypothesis_checks: The Euclidean Lebesgue space is a measurable space with measure dx; ℝ is a normed additive commutative group and real normed space.
F003 gives almost everywhere strong measurability of each V(k), from its continuity.
F003 and F002 give integrability of w, since it is B times the indicator of the finite-measure box Q.
F003 gives the pointwise bound |V(k)(x)|≤w(x), which implies the required almost everywhere bounds.
F003 gives convergence to e_t(x,t0) at every x from time differentiability, hence almost everywhere.

Fix an arbitrary spatial coordinate j from 1 through n.
Choose C from N002 at t0, jointly with R and the accompanying bounds.

iota(y,r) inserts r as the j-th coordinate and the coordinates of y in their original order as the remaining coordinates.

locals.type: family of real functions indexed by ℝ^(n−1)
locals.declaration: Define phi(y)(r)=g(iota(y,r)).
Set Qrest=[−R,R]^(n−1), with the singleton convention in dimension zero.

argument.text:
Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0, and fix any spatial coordinate j with 1≤j≤n (H001). Choose C,R from N002 at this time and set Q=[−R,R]^n. Put g(x)=u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0). It is smooth by H002. Since C is compact and contained in the open box (−R,R)^n, it has positive distance from the boundary of Q; N002 therefore makes g zero on a neighborhood of that boundary. The product rule gives
∂_{x_j}g(x)=∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)+u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0).
N002 says the derivative and each summand are continuous, supported in C, and integrable on ℝ^n and hence on Q.

produces.statement: g is smooth and zero near the boundary of Q. Its derivative ∂_{x_j}g=∂_{x_j}u_t(·,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(·,t0)+u_t(·,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(·,t0); the derivative and both summands are supported in C and absolutely integrable.

argument.text:
Let iota(y,r) insert the real r in coordinate j, with y∈ℝ^(n−1) giving all remaining coordinates in their original order, and put phi(y)(r)=g(iota(y,r)). For each y, phi(y) is smooth on ℝ with derivative r↦∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)). Its endpoint values at −R and R are zero, since those points have a coordinate on the boundary of Q and in any event lie outside C. Apply M003 with real codomain, endpoints −R,R, function phi(y), and the displayed derivative. The derivative exists at every point of [−R,R] and is continuous, hence interval integrable there. We obtain
∫_{−R}^{R} ∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) dr=phi(y)(R)−phi(y)(−R)=0.
This holds for every y∈ℝ^(n−1). The oriented integral agrees with the Lebesgue integral on the closed interval here, since −R<R and the endpoints have measure zero.

Set Qrest=[−R,R]^(n−1). Under iota, Qrest×[−R,R] is exactly Q with its coordinates reordered. Standard Lebesgue measure is the product of the coordinate measures (D001); reordering these factors preserves the measure, since on any coordinate rectangle both descriptions give the product of the same side lengths. Thus the integral on Q is the product-measure integral of (y,r)↦∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) with Lebesgue measures restricted to Qrest and [−R,R]. This scalar function is continuous on a compact box and bounded there, hence integrable for that finite product measure. M002 now gives
∫_Q ∂_{x_j}g dx=∫_{Qrest}(∫_{[−R,R]}∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)) dr) dy=0
by F002. When n=1, Qrest is the singleton ℝ^0 of measure one, so this formula reduces to the very same one-variable identity. Outside Q all terms in F001 vanish. Integrating F001 over ℝ^n, using the finiteness of both summand integrals and symmetry of the dot product, yields
∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0) dx=−∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0) dx.
Quantify the arbitrary coordinate j, discharge L1, and quantify t0. This proves the claimed integration-by-parts identity including absolute integrability.

applications.bindings: For every fixed remaining-coordinate vector y, take V=ℝ, a=−R, b=R, f=phi(y), and f'(r)=∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)).
hypothesis_checks: ℝ is a complete normed additive commutative group and real normed space.
F001 gives global smoothness of g; coordinate insertion is affine, so the stated derivative of phi(y) exists on all of [−R,R], including endpoints.
The derivative is continuous on the compact interval, and therefore Lebesgue interval integrable.

applications.bindings: Take A=ℝ^(n−1), B=ℝ, μ=Lebesgue measure restricted to Qrest, ν=Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R], V=ℝ, and f(y,r)=∂_{x_j}g(iota(y,r)). Use the coordinate-product identification of Q explained in S003.
hypothesis_checks: The Borel/Lebesgue measurable coordinate spaces carry the stated measures; their restrictions to these boxes are finite and hence s-finite, also for n=1 with the measure-one singleton factor.
The scalar codomain ℝ has the required normed additive commutative group and real normed-space structures.
F001 gives continuity of the derivative; composed with iota it is bounded and measurable on this finite-measure compact product box, which proves product integrability before applying M002.

Fix any real s.

argument.text:
Fix real t0 and assume L1: t0>0. H002 makes all derivative notation classical. N002 proves e(·,t0) and all derivative products below are integrable, so E is the finite energy integral in D004. N003 proves differentiability and its integral formula. Substitute that formula and use N004 for each coordinate, then use finite-sum linearity and the definition of Delta:
E'(t0)=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·u_tt(x,t0) dx+2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t0) dx
=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·u_tt(x,t0) dx−2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_jx_j}u(x,t0) dx
=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t(x,t0)·(u_tt(x,t0)−Delta u(x,t0)) dx=0.
The last equality is N001 pointwise. Every passage uses finite integrals from N002, with no boundary term left over. Discharge L1 and universally quantify t0. Hence E is differentiable everywhere on (0,∞) with E'=0 there.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary real s,t and assume L2: 0<s<t. Apply M004 to the real function equal to E on positive times and zero elsewhere, with derivative function zero, and endpoints s,t. By F001, E is differentiable at every point of [s,t], so it is continuous there and has derivative zero on (s,t). M004 gives an interior point whose derivative zero equals (E(t)−E(s))/(t−s). Since t−s>0, E(t)=E(s). Discharge L2 and quantify s,t. Any pair of positive times is either equal or can be ordered in this way, so symmetry of equality gives constancy on (0,∞). Together with N002 and F001 this proves P. The density is exactly |u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|² from D003, so no factor 1/2 is introduced and no assertion at time zero is used.

applications.bindings: Take f(r)=E(r) for r>0 and f(r)=0 for r≤0; take f'(r)=0 for all real r; set a=s and b=t.
hypothesis_checks: F001 gives differentiability at each point of [s,t]⊂(0,∞), hence continuity there; the extension equals E throughout a neighborhood of that interval.
